- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 30d mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > 0.0) and price is trending down, model frequently fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average.
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often underestimates the decline; increase forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “zero” or near-zero sentiment, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; add ±0.5% noise to forecast for days with no sentiment signal.
